subject: Is it possible to use multiple processors (or cpus) to speed up linkage mapping process?

messages.author: 87af66513dd507f5
messages.subject: Is it possible to use multiple processors (or cpus) to speed up linkage mapping process?
parts:
Hello,
I am wondering if there is a way to speed up some steps in RQTL genetic mapping procedure such such ordermarker(). On my local computer (Lenovo Workstation, Intel Xeon, 12 CPUs and 64 GB RAM), it takes a few days to complete ordering while biggest group which has 400 or so markers don't get completed because of memory limitation error. I do have access to use HPC cluster with more memory and CPUs but just wanted to know if it is possible to use multiple processor at the same time or it just uses single processor? If I am not wrong then n.cluster arguments in some functions such as ripple() does the same thing but can we use it for all functions (or at least functions I am concerned about orderMarker() and Tryallpositions())?

Thank you so much in advance for any information in this regard
Prashant

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Is it possible to use multiple processors (or cpus) to speed up linkage mapping process?
parts:
orderMarkers can be easily parallelized, except to split by chromosome. tryAllPositions could be, but I’m currently focusing on developing R/qtl2 and am not planning to implement further features in R/qtl, except maintenance and bug fixes.

You might look at other packages, such as ASMap.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Is it possible to use multiple processors (or cpus) to speed up linkage mapping process?
parts:
Oops; sorry...I meant the opposite of what I said. orderMarkers can **not** be easily parallelized. It’s adding a marker at a time to the map; each has to wait for the results of the previous.

karl
